passage: Dear diary, today in front of the whole class I called Siddharth "Pimple", and everyone laughed. He went quiet and stared at his shoes. It did not feel as good as I thought it would. I know why I do it. I am the shortest boy in Class 6, and every day I wait for someone to start on me. So I go first, and then nobody can. But tonight I keep thinking about Siddharth's face. Maybe I could sit with Ravi and the chess boys instead. They don't do this stuff. And maybe I can stop hating my height so much. -- Manoj

qa.q: What did Manoj call Siddharth in front of the class?
Why does Manoj tease others about their looks before anyone can tease him?
qa.a: He is scared of being teased about being the shortest, so he strikes first, hoping that way nobody can start on him.

qa.q: What could Manoj try instead of attacking first?
qa.a: He could sit with kinder friends, such as the chess boys, and work on feeling okay about himself rather than picking on others.

qa.q: How might Siddharth have felt when the class laughed?
qa.a: Siddharth probably felt embarrassed and hurt, since he went quiet and stared at his shoes.

grounding: A child who teases others about their looks because he dreads being teased sees the pattern and plans a kinder way.

passage:
In their Siliguri school, Bidisha always spoke first. "Nice frizz, Ganga. Did you sleep in a bush?" The girls around her laughed.
What they didn't know: Bidisha spent every morning in the bathroom mirror, checking the gap in her teeth, terrified someone would notice. If she mocked first, maybe no one would look at her.
Then one day Ganga turned round. "You always do this before anyone can say anything about you, don't you?"
Bidisha's face burned. She had no answer.
That weekend she started art club instead of hanging out with the laughing girls. Nobody there cared about teeth. Slowly she smiled more, gap and all.

qa.q: What did Bidisha say about Ganga's hair?
qa.a: "Nice frizz, Ganga. Did you sleep in a bush?"

qa.q: What was Bidisha afraid of every morning?
qa.a: She was terrified someone would notice the gap in her teeth, and mocking others first felt like protection.

qa.q: What wiser way did Bidisha start to find?
qa.a: She joined art club with kinder people and slowly built real confidence, smiling more with the gap.

qa.q: How might Ganga see Bidisha's teasing?
qa.a: Ganga sees through it, recognising that Bidisha attacks first to stop people noticing her.

grounding: A girl teases others about their looks because she dreads being teased herself; when called out, she builds real confidence and finds kinder friends.

passage:
"Why do you always joke about people's glasses?" Maria asked, walking home.
Nazia shrugged. "It's funny."
"Is it?"
Nazia was quiet. Then: "If I say something first, nobody says anything about my ears."
"Your ears?"
"They stick out. Someone called me 'jug' in Class 3. I never want that again."
Maria stopped walking. "So you hurt people so they won't hurt you?"
Nazia's eyes stung. "I guess."
"That's a lot of work. Come to drama club with me? Nobody cares about ears there. And I like your laugh, when it's not at someone."
Nazia wiped her eyes and smiled a little. "Okay."

qa.q: What did someone call Nazia in Class 3?
Why does Nazia joke about people's glasses?
qa.a: She is afraid of being teased about her ears again, so she attacks first to protect herself.

qa.q: What did Maria suggest that could help Nazia?
qa.a: She suggested drama club, a kinder group where Nazia could build confidence without needing to mock others.

qa.q: How might Maria see Nazia after this talk?
qa.a: Maria seems to understand her better and still likes her, especially her laugh when it's not at someone.

grounding: A girl mocks others' looks because she dreads being teased herself; a friend gently names it and invites her to a kinder group.
